goal_tracker.message: You need 38.0 more km across 9 sessions in the remaining 30 days to match last month’s volume. That averages to ~1.27 km per day or ~4.2 km every 3 days — achievable with 3–4 runs/week (e.g., three 4.5 km runs + one 5.0 km run).

insights.title: Efficiency stable but pace-HR mismatch evident
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency (13.66) and VO2 max (35–36 mL/kg/min) are stable, yet recent runs show wide pace variation (7:13 to 14:00 min/km) with minimal HR change (120–144 bpm), suggesting inconsistent effort calibration — especially the 14:00 min/km run at only 120 bpm (likely recovery walk-run or low-effort session misrecorded as run).

insights.title: Zone 3 dominates — aerobic base may be underdeveloped
insights.body: HR zone distribution shows 26% in Zone 3 (threshold), 32% in Zone 2 (aerobic), and only 23% in Zone 1 (recovery). This inverted pyramid — with more time in Z3 than Z2 — risks premature fatigue and limits mitochondrial adaptation; optimal base-building for recreational runners typically targets ≥45% Z2 time.

insights.title: Cadence-stride trade-off observed during faster efforts
insights.body: At 7:13 min/km (428 sec/km), cadence rises to 150 spm and stride length jumps to 91.78 cm — a 26% increase from the 7:47 min/km run (72.88 cm). While efficient at speed, this large stride surge correlates with higher vertical oscillation (8.8 cm vs. 6.4–8.2 cm elsewhere), increasing impact stress.

insights.title: Low ground contact time variability signals consistent neuromuscular output
insights.body: Ground contact time ranges narrowly from 298–327 ms across recent runs (mean 311 ms), indicating stable leg spring stiffness and rhythm — a positive sign of consistency despite pace fluctuations. This suggests good day-to-day readiness and neuromuscular control.

recommendations.action: Do your next run as a pure Zone 2 aerobic session: 5.0 km at avg HR ≤135 bpm, cadence 142–146 spm, pace between 9:00–10:30 min/km — use the 2026-04-26 run (120 bpm, 14:00 min/km) as a lower-bound reference but aim for *higher* intensity within Z2.
recommendations.reason: Z2 currently makes up only 32% of HR time — increasing deliberate Z2 volume will strengthen aerobic base, improve efficiency, and support future Z3/Z4 work.

recommendations.action: Perform a 3 × 3-min progressive cadence drill before your next 4–5 km run: start at 142 spm (metronome), increase by 3 spm each interval (145 → 148 → 151), holding form and minimizing vertical oscillation (<8.0 cm).
recommendations.reason: Cadence increased to 150+ spm during faster runs, but vertical oscillation rose to 8.8 cm — targeted cadence drills reinforce neuromuscular efficiency without sacrificing bounce control.

recommendations.action: Replace one weekly run with a 30-min easy Zone 1–2 walk-run (e.g., 2-min walk / 3-min jog x6), targeting avg HR 115–125 bpm and cadence ~130 spm, to safely increase Z1 time and reduce cumulative impact.
recommendations.reason: Z1 accounts for only 23% of HR time — adding structured low-intensity volume improves recovery capacity and capillary density without raising injury risk.

weekly_focus.description: Prioritize time-in-zone discipline and neuromuscular consistency over pace or distance. Focus on building Z2 volume, refining cadence-stride harmony, and restoring Z1 recovery capacity.
suggested_sessions: 4 km easy run with cadence drills
